newsitem.title: SOMALIA: Nine killed in fighting in southern Somalia port.
newsitem.headline: Nine killed in fighting in southern Somalia port.

text.p: At least nine people were killed and ten wounded when dozens of armed men attacked shops, restaurants and businesses in the southern Somali port of Kismayu on Saturday night, residents reported.
They said the attackers were from the Marehan clan of former dictator Mohamed Siad Barre, who was ousted in a civil war early in 1991 and later died in exile.
Witnesses said the attackers fired indiscriminately at people who were relaxing, drinking tea or listening to the radio, at 9.15 p.m. (1815 GMT) -- nearly three hours after sunset.
The attack was linked to a long-standing feud between the Majertein clan militia who control Kismayu and the Marehan, based 18 km (12 miles) north of the port, residents said.
Radio reports said hundreds of women and children demonstrated on Sunday, condemning the attackers and calling on their men to defend them.
They stoned unarmed young men and shouted at them to go and fight the Marehan.
Later reports said a revenge attack had been launched against the Marehan militia at their base. No details of casualties were available.
The Marehan were driven out of Kismayu early this year after their enemies accused them of supporting Somali warlord Hussein Mohamed Aideed, who has his base 500 km (300 miles) north in Mogadishu.

In Mogadishu on Sunday thousands attended a rally marking the second anniversary of the government set up by Aideed's late father, Mohamed Farah Aideed. The Aideed "government" has not been recognised by other countries, but is supported by some Somali factions.
Speaking at the rally, Aideed condemned last week's incursion into western Somalia by Ethiopian armed forces, who still control the towns of Bulo Hawo and Luq.

Somalia has had no effective government since the Siad Barre regime collapsed in 1991. Armed factions control different areas, and the northern half of the country has seceded and declared itself the Republic of Somaliland.
